newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice futures end lower after very quiet day.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice futures end lower after very quiet day.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended with modest losses in old crop contracts Monday, while new crop contracts showed steeper losses on hedge pressure, traders said.
"We saw some selling interest in new crop, and I'm pretty sure it was tied to hedging," one pit trader said.
LIT America and Dean Witter were early sellers and late buyers in the rice market, pit sources said.
Traders awaited news of a Costa Rican rice tender. Results were expected as early as Monday afternoon, and one U.S. exporter said the business could go to the U.S.

Traders also took note of news that China has signed a memorandum of understanding to buy 1.03 million tonnes of rice from Thailand. Further details of the deal were not yet available, Thai government officials said.
Rice ended 12 per cwt lower to steady, with May off 1-2/2 at $11.66-1/2 and July steady at $11.68.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 300 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 302 lots.
